LESSON: MOSAIC

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENTS
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.5: Mosaic
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Mosaic, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENTS.

Key inquiry question: Why do you paste coloured papers in mosaic? 2. How do you make mosaic?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Mosaic together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learners exchange ideas as they talk about or sign own and others’ mosaic work.

• Imagination and creativity: The learners express themselves through mosaic picture making.

• Self-efficacy: Learner express themselves about their artwork during display sessions.

• Digital Literacy: Learner explore digital devices for mosaic images..

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Life skills: Learners develop self-awareness and self-esteem through display of their work and guiding them to express their

feelings, ideas and emotions.

• ESD: Learner takes care for the environment as source of materials and tools for mosaic.

Link to other learning areas:

• Environmental Activities: The learner recycles waste materials from the environment to make mosaic pictures.

• Health Education: Learners observe safety when collecting and using different types of locally available materials and tools

from the environment.

• Language activities: Learners learn the word Mosaic as a vocabulary in language activities.

Suggested learning resources.

Waste papers, scissors, glue, colours, dry grass, beads.
